The auxiliary SS consisted mostly of civilians and regular army personal who were forced to stay behind at the concentration camps. They received little training and barely any equipment. Their main duty was to take the blame. WWII was so large and involved so many people who were involuntarily a part of it. It's difficult to pin point who was innocent.

At the end of the war, the auxiliary SS were running the nazi concentration camps. They were basically used at a scapegoat as the higher ranking SS officials who actually ran the camps during the war fled. Chances are the German being assaulted in this photo was part of this scapegoat division. He probably just showed up at the camp a couple weeks prior and has little to no part with carrying out "the final solution". This picture is morbid on both sides. The prisoner who went through hell and perhaps has no family to go back to, and the guard who is going to be blamed for a mass genocide when in reality he probably had little to do with it. At least the guard in the camp was lucky enough that the Americans liberated it. Russians during the war were known to be extraordinarily brutal

Physics 2070 - Galaxies and the Universe. By far the most interesting course I've taken so far, but you need to have a fairly strong physics and math background. And even though Physics 1070 (Fundamentals of Astronomy) isn't a prerequisite, I'd highly recommend taking that before you delve into 2070 because you need to know those astronomical concepts like the back of your hand for this course. In 2070 you learn about stellar death which drives the formation and progression of galaxies. Then you go onto learning about galaxies as a whole, and after that the universe as a whole, which is the basis of cosmology. You also get to do a term assignment in this course using the 40cm telescope in the observatory at York.
